title: KRDPASS Auth SDK Redirect URI Validation Test Vectors
description: Canonical redirect-response validation cases shared by KRDPASS Auth SDK integrations.

rule.summary: A response must use HTTPS and the configured redirect origin and encoded path. Query parameters registered on the redirect URI must be preserved exactly; single-valued authorization-response metadata is ignored.
details: Configured and incoming redirect URIs must use HTTPS, have a non-empty host, and contain neither userinfo nor a fragment.
The incoming URI must match the configured URI's normalized scheme, host, and effective port.
The incoming URI's encoded path must exactly match the configured URI's encoded path; host-only matching is not sufficient.
Every query parameter registered on the redirect URI must be present with the same value and multiplicity in the response URI.
Unconfigured authorization-response parameters may occur once and are ignored, as required by OAuth. Duplicate parameters and extra occurrences of configured query names are rejected.
A security response parameter that is present but blank (empty or whitespace only, with or without an '=') is malformed and rejected.

error_description and error_uri are deliberately not security response parameters. They are display strings shown to the user, never inputs to a security decision, so a blank one is cosmetic rather than malformed and must not fail the callback.
A response carrying both code and error is ambiguous and is rejected, so that the order in which an implementation checks the two branches can never decide the outcome.

Percent escapes must be syntactically well formed. Byte sequences that are well formed as escapes but are not valid UTF-8 are decoded lossily (U+FFFD) rather than rejected; rejecting them needs byte-level URI parsing and is out of scope for redirect matching.
Authorization-server registration remains the final authority for exact redirect URI matching. These client-side checks are defence in depth.

vectors.reason: The configured URI itself is a valid response target.

vectors.description: Configured path with OAuth response parameters
vectors.reason: OAuth response parameters may be appended to the exact configured redirect URI.

vectors.description: Configured path with an OAuth error response
vectors.reason: OAuth error response parameters may be appended to the exact configured redirect URI.
An OAuth response parameter may occur only once to prevent ambiguous parsing.

vectors.description: Same host with a different callback path
vectors.reason: The encoded path must exactly match the configured redirect URI.

vectors.description: Same host with the root path
vectors.reason: Host-only matching is insufficient; the configured callback path is required.

vectors.description: Configured path with OpenID Connect session metadata
vectors.reason: The endpoint still matches exactly and OAuth clients ignore unrecognized single-valued response parameters.
Authorization response parameters must not be included more than once.

vectors.description: Configured fixed query parameters are retained while OAuth response parameters are appended
vectors.reason: Registered query parameters are preserved and OAuth response parameters are appended.

vectors.description: Configured fixed query parameter is missing
vectors.reason: Every registered query parameter must be preserved.

vectors.description: Configured fixed query parameter value changed
vectors.reason: Registered query parameter values are part of the redirect URI.

vectors.description: Configured fixed query parameter multiplicity changed
vectors.reason: Registered query parameter multiplicity must be preserved.
Only HTTPS redirect URIs are permitted.
Only HTTPS redirect URIs are permitted.
A host is required.
The normalized host must match the configured redirect URI.
Subdomains are distinct redirect hosts.
The effective port is part of the redirect URI authority.

vectors.description: Case variation in scheme and host
vectors.reason: URL scheme and host comparison are case-insensitive.
IPv4 hosts are supported when the exact path also matches.
IPv6 hosts are supported when the exact path also matches.

vectors.description: RFC 9207 iss appended to the configured redirect URI
vectors.reason: iss is an authorization response parameter. Whether its value is the expected issuer is decided by the issuerVectors contract, not by redirect matching.
iss is a security response parameter: present but blank is malformed.
A whitespace-only security response parameter is blank, not a value.

vectors.description: iss with no value at all
vectors.reason: A security response parameter with no '=' carries no value and is rejected.

vectors.description: Response carrying both code and error
vectors.reason: A response carrying both code and error is ambiguous; branch order must never decide the outcome.

vectors.description: Response parameter value whose percent escapes are not valid UTF-8
vectors.reason: %FF is a well formed percent escape that is not valid UTF-8. It is decoded lossily to U+FFFD and accepted; only syntactically malformed escapes are rejected.

issuerRule.summary: RFC 9207: when an authorization response carrying a code also carries iss, the percent-decoded iss must exactly equal the environment's authorization server URL. An absent iss is accepted.
details: The comparison is exact string equality after percent-decoding. Trailing slashes, case, and ports are not normalised, matching how the SDKs already compare the id_token iss claim against the same environment value.
iss is compared only on the success branch. CAS omits iss on error responses, and an error response delivers no credential to bind to an issuer.
An absent iss must not fail: requiring it would reject every CAS error callback.
A present-but-blank iss never reaches this comparison; the redirect-response rule above rejects it first as invalid_redirect.

issuerVectors.description: Percent-encoded iss equal to the production authorization server
issuerVectors.reason: This is the shape CAS actually sends: iss last and percent-encoded.

issuerVectors.description: Literal iss equal to the production authorization server
issuerVectors.reason: Percent-encoding of the iss value is not significant; the decoded value is compared.

issuerVectors.description: iss from an unrelated authorization server
issuerVectors.reason: A code from a different authorization server is a mix-up attack and is rejected fail-closed.

issuerVectors.description: Development issuer on a production configuration
issuerVectors.reason: The expected issuer comes from the configured environment, not from a fixed constant.

issuerVectors.description: Expected issuer with a trailing slash
issuerVectors.reason: The comparison is exact; issuer identifiers are not URL-normalised.

issuerVectors.description: Development issuer on a development configuration
issuerVectors.reason: The development environment's authorization server URL is the expected issuer there.

issuerVectors.description: Success response with no iss at all
issuerVectors.reason: iss is optional: an authorization server that does not support RFC 9207 must still work.

issuerVectors.description: Error response with no iss at all
issuerVectors.reason: CAS omits iss on error responses; requiring it would break every error callback.

issuerVectors.description: Error response carrying an unrelated iss
issuerVectors.reason: The error branch delivers no credential to bind to an issuer, so iss is not compared there.
